montu-mia.title: Montu Mia's System Design
montu-mia.description: System design as a story, in Bengali first, English second. 3,000+ subscribers, 30,000+ visitors, 125,000+ page views, 147 GitHub stars.
montu-mia.longDescription: Montu Mia is trying to keep a video site alive. Each chapter is a problem he hits, load balancers, caches, CDNs, the trade-off that didn't fit on the first slide. I publish it as a site and a LinkedIn newsletter. Bengali is the default. English lives under /en. Email goes out through AWS SES. The site list has 1,100+ subscribers. LinkedIn has 2,600+. OG images are generated per chapter. The reading UI is Fumadocs and MDX.
features: Chapters in Bengali, with English chapter by chapter
Email newsletter through AWS SES and React Email
OG image per chapter
Dark and light reading UI
Untranslated pages fall back to Bengali
challenges: SES plus React Email without turning into a deliverability hobby
OG images that still look like the chapter
LLM translation that kept Montu's jokes, then a lot of hand edits
Making Fumadocs read like a book, not a docs site
impact: 3,000+ subscribers across the site and LinkedIn
1,100+ on the site list, 2,600+ on LinkedIn
30,000+ unique visitors, 125,000+ page views
147 GitHub stars

trak.title: trak.sh
trak.description: Link analytics for a newsletter issue. Which story got clicks, grouped, plus file drops with expiring links.
trak.longDescription: I write a newsletter. After I send an issue I want to know which story got clicks, as a group, not a pile of naked URLs. No shortener did that, so I built one. trak.sh tags links to an issue, has a free tier, a REST API, and Drops for private files with an expiry. I run Montu Mia through it every week.
features: Analytics grouped by issue or campaign
Short links with no signup on the free plan
Drops: private files, expiring download links
REST API, UTM presets, tags, QR codes, public stats
Custom domains and CSV export on Pro
challenges: Grouping clicks by issue, not by URL
A free plan that still does the job
File sharing on top of a shortener without a second product
impact: I use it every week on Montu Mia
Free plan, Pro at $6 a month

type-win.title: type.win
type-win.description: A typing arcade. Word Fall, Type Race, a daily quote. Best on a keyboard.
type-win.longDescription: Most typing tests look like forms. type.win is an arcade instead. Word Fall drops words from the sky. Type Race is a live WPM race. There is one daily quote, same run for everyone that UTC day. Keyboard first. Desktop is the point.
features: Word Fall: type incoming words or lose
Type Race: live WPM against other people
Daily quote, one shared run per UTC day
Leaderboards and profiles
challenges: Making a typing game feel like a cabinet, not a quiz
Races that stay fair when the network is not
impact: Live at type.win

ramble.title: Ramble
ramble.description: Peaches is the meeting agent inside Ramble. I own that feature. Python, TypeScript, React, Swift. Internal beta. No outside users yet.
ramble.longDescription: Peaches sits in the meeting. Wake it, join from the calendar, keep a session, write notes and checklists. It lives inside Ramble. I own that feature. Python services, the web client, native Swift on macOS and iPhone. Other engineers review and test.
features: Wake and sleep, plus transcript buffering for live meetings
Tools that write notes and checklists
Calendar auto-join with durable persistence and verified webhooks
Cross-device presence and failure-state feedback from macOS
On-device transcription and editable notes on iPhone
challenges: Keeping a Mac app, an iPhone client, and a web app on the same session without fighting each other
Making calendar auto-join reliable when bots, webhooks, and short-lived credentials all have to agree
A voice loop that feels instant without dumping raw audio into a chat window
impact: Internal beta on Mac, iPhone, and web
No outside users yet
One session model across native apps, web, and backend

claudebar.title: ClaudeBar
claudebar.description: Mac menu bar. Claude Code usage, stats, which model you burned.
claudebar.longDescription: ClaudeBar sits in the Mac menu bar and shows how I've been using Claude Code. Usage, stats, model split. I also published the skill I used to build it, a Claude Code skill for single-file SwiftUI menubar apps.
features: Claude Code usage in the menu bar
Model breakdown
A Claude Code skill for other menubar apps
challenges: Useful stats in a strip of pixels, not another dashboard
Turning the pattern into a skill someone else can run
impact: I glance at it while I work
The menubar skill is public

avro-silicon.title: Avro Silicon
avro-silicon.description: Avro phonetic keyboard, rebuilt for Apple Silicon after macOS said the old one would die.
avro-silicon.longDescription: I type Bengali in Avro every day. The Mac build had not been touched in years, no Apple Silicon, and macOS started warning it would break. I don't write Objective-C or InputMethodKit for a living. I sat down with Claude Code, rebuilt it for arm64, ripped out CocoaPods and a couple of dead libraries, and fixed a suggestion bug that made typing lag. I did not open a PR on the original repo. Dumping a pile of AI code on a maintainer I can't help later is rude. The fork builds from source.
features: Native Apple Silicon, arm64
Phonetic Bengali typing
System keyboard
Unicode normalization, more tests, CI
challenges: Touching a legacy input method without breaking tomorrow's typing
Replacing CocoaPods, RegexKitLite, and FMDB with system frameworks
Being honest about AI-written code
impact: Bengali phonetic typing still works on M-series Macs
Build from source. Signing and notarization still need someone with a paid Apple account.

vocables.title: Vocables
vocables.description: Vocab practice for IELTS, GRE, TOEFL, SAT. Suggestions, quizzes, a list you review.
vocables.longDescription: I wanted exam vocab that was not a flashcard dump. Vocables suggests words for a level and a test, quizzes you, and keeps a list to review. Next.js, Clerk, Polar, Vercel AI SDK. Mostly vibe-coded.
features: Word suggestions for a level and an exam
IELTS, GRE, TOEFL, SAT
Quizzes
Save and review
challenges: A product, not a word list with a login
Tying suggestions to a specific exam
impact: Live at vocables.xyz

profreach.title: Profreach
profreach.description: Track which professors you emailed, so the spreadsheet doesn't rot.
profreach.longDescription: Finding professors, writing to them, then forgetting who got the email three weeks ago. The spreadsheet version of this always dies. Profreach is a small tracker for that process.
features: Find professors
Track outreach
Keep the threads in one place
challenges: Simple enough that someone will open it twice
Many threads, without becoming a CRM
impact: Live at profreach.shakirul.dev

coterm.title: Coterm
coterm.description: English in, CLI command out. Rust, a Vercel edge function, OpenAI. Asks before it runs something dumb.
coterm.longDescription: I know what I want. I forget the flags. Coterm takes English, gives a command, lets you edit it, then runs it on a keypress. Rust client, OpenAI behind a Vercel edge function, and a check for commands that can wreck a disk.
features: English to a CLI command
Edit the command before you run it
Warns on dangerous commands
One key to run, after you confirm
challenges: A command that is useful and not reckless
Edit in place
Run on one key after a confirm
Keep the model call on the edge
impact: Public releases on GitHub
Useful when someone freezes at the prompt

resume.title: Re:sume
resume.description: Resume builder. GPT for the writing, PDF out the other end.
resume.longDescription: Re:sume was the resume product at Re:cruit. Create a resume, keep versions in Postgres, ask GPT to punch up the writing, export a PDF. Next.js, Prisma, React PDF.
features: GPT for the bullet points
Create and view resumes
PDF export
Versions in the database
challenges: Prompts that didn't sound like a robot wrote the resume
PDF layout that survived other people's life stories
An editor people finished
impact: People left with a PDF

bochon.title: Bochon
bochon.description: Click a Bengali speech-to-text model, hear it, compare the scores. Built for Bengali.AI.
bochon.longDescription: Bochon is a dashboard for Bengali.AI. Pick a Bengali ASR model, run a clip, see the numbers next to the others. TypeScript, React, Chakra, Python, Docker, Nginx.
features: Side by side model scores
Try a clip in the browser
Accuracy numbers
Live inference
challenges: Audio in the browser without a mess
Charts that don't lie about a close race
A layout that still works when the table is ugly
impact: Bengali.AI could compare ASR models without a spreadsheet
